_comment: Derived seed — canonical source is 'The Charter Queue — Factual Timeline' (Cross-cuts). Re-run build_charter_seed.py after editing it. Never hand-edit this file.

items.title: Fnality International is established
items.entities: Fnality International Limited; shareholder banks
items.summary: A private company limited by shares, England and Wales, owned by a consortium of banks and market utilities. Its purpose is the one thing no stablecoin can offer: a settlement asset that *is* central-bank money, held in a pooled omnibus account at the Bank of England.

items.title: Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A. receives the first digital-asset national trust charter
items.entities: OCC; Anchor Labs; Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.
items.summary: The OCC charters the first national trust bank built for digital assets, under a 2021 operating agreement. Five years later it is still the only member of the cohort that has been a chartered, operating national bank the whole way through. A trust charter is not a commercial-bank charter: no insured deposits, no lending, no discount window, and no Federal Reserve master account.

items.title: Partior is founded by DBS, J.P. Morgan and Temasek
items.entities: Partior; DBS; J.P. Morgan; Temasek; Standard Chartered
items.summary: Out of the Monetary Authority of Singapore's Project Ubin. The settled asset is tokenized **commercial-bank money** — a liability of the participating settlement bank, not of Partior, and not of any central bank. Whoever the money is owed by is the whole question.

items.title: The sterling Fnality Payment System is recognized as a UK payment system
items.entities: Fnality UK Limited; HM Treasury; Bank of England
items.summary: Formal recognition. The pooled central-bank funds sit in trust in a Bank of England RTGS omnibus account. This is the only place in the whole sweep where a private tokenized rail settles in genuine central-bank money — and it took an act of national recognition to get there.

items.title: The sterling Fnality system makes its first payments
items.entities: Fnality UK Limited; Lloyds; Santander; UBS
items.summary: Three banks, an initial proving phase. Live — in the narrowest of the five senses of that word.

items.title: Canton Coin genesis
items.entities: Canton Network; Canton Foundation; Digital Asset
items.summary: No premine, no presale, no founder or venture allocation. The network is not owned by the company that builds its technology — a distinction the sweep insists on and most reporting collapses.

items.title: The sterling Fnality system operates under Bank of England limits
items.entities: Fnality UK Limited; Bank of England
items.summary: The Bank's own classification, and it controls over any marketing language. The scaling gate is a supervisory permission, not a technical milestone — one regulator's decision stands between this and the whole "central-bank money on chain" pitch.

items.title: Stripe completes its acquisition of Bridge
items.entities: Stripe; Bridge
items.summary: The merchant-payments giant pulls stablecoin orchestration inside the house. Wallet infrastructure (Privy), a proprietary chain (Tempo) and a proposed trust bank follow. The pattern of the whole era in one deal: buy the missing layer, do not build a coalition.

items.title: Kinexys, Chainlink and Ondo complete a cross-chain delivery-versus-payment test
items.entities: J.P. Morgan Kinexys; Chainlink; Ondo
items.summary: Ondo's tokenized Treasuries formed the asset leg; **J.P. Morgan deposits** formed the payment leg. A transaction path was proved. A production service was not.

items.title: Fiserv announces FIUSD
items.entities: Fiserv
items.summary: A stablecoin marketed into the core banking and merchant systems Fiserv already runs. Thirteen months later the public record still does not name the issuer, the redemption obligor or the reserve custodian. A coin with no stated debtor is not yet a coin.

items.title: Digital Asset raises $135 million
items.entities: Digital Asset; DRW; Tradeweb; DTCC; Goldman Sachs; Citadel Securities; BNP Paribas; Circle Ventures; Paxos; Virtu
items.summary: The dealers, the market makers, the banks, **the depository itself**, and the crypto firms all buy into the company that builds Canton. When DTCC is an investor in the ledger that will carry DTC's tokens, "disruption" is not the word for what is happening.

items.title: Ripple and the SEC dismiss their appeals; the judgment stands
items.entities: Ripple Labs; SEC; U.S. District Court (S.D.N.Y.)
items.summary: The district court's final judgment survives: a **$125,035,150** civil penalty and an injunction against unregistered institutional offers and sales. The long war ends not in vindication but in a paid fine and a standing injunction — and Ripple turns immediately toward the charter.

items.title: NYDFS fines Paxos $26.5 million over the Binance relationship
items.entities: NYDFS; Paxos Trust Company
items.summary: A $26.5M penalty plus $22M of mandated compliance investment, for historic anti-money-laundering and transaction-monitoring failures around the BUSD partnership. The lesson the sweep draws is the one that matters: **a regulated issuer can keep its reserves perfectly and still fail at watching its distributor.** Backing is not oversight.

items.title: Anchorage files a Federal Reserve access request
items.entities: Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.; Federal Reserve
items.summary: Tier 3. It is the most advanced request in the entire cohort, filed by the only member with a five-year-old national charter. **As of the Fed database's currency date of 2026-05-31 it is still pending** — nine months, no answer, no denial. This single line is the whole private stack's position in one fact.

items.title: Fnality closes a $136 million Series C
items.entities: Fnality International; WisdomTree; Bank of America; Citi; KBC; Temasek; Tradeweb; Santander; Barclays; BNP Paribas; DTCC; Euroclear; Goldman Sachs; ING; Nasdaq Ventures; State Street; UBS
items.summary: Twenty-four institutions. The money is not betting on a token; it is betting on the one rail that touches a central bank's balance sheet.

items.title: Chainlink becomes a Canton Super Validator
items.entities: Chainlink Labs; Canton Network; Canton Foundation
items.summary: The neutral connector takes a governance seat on the network it connects. The middleware vendor is now a governed market participant with a vote. The sweep flags the conflict plainly; nobody has resolved it.

items.title: Deutsche Bank completes the first live euro cross-border payment on Partior
items.entities: Deutsche Bank; DBS; Partior
items.summary: Real money, real corridor. Each settlement bank still issues its own liability — the ledger is shared, the debt is not.

items.title: Ripple closes the Hidden Road acquisition; it becomes Ripple Prime
items.entities: Ripple; Hidden Road; Ripple Prime
items.summary: $1.25 billion for a prime brokerage. With Metaco and Standard Custody (custody), Rail (payments) and GTreasury (corporate treasury), Ripple has bought itself an end-to-end institutional money circuit. What it still does not have is an account at the Federal Reserve.

items.title: Paxos announces the acquisition of Fordefi
items.entities: Paxos; Fordefi
items.summary: Institutional wallet and custody infrastructure, pulled inside. The missing layer, bought rather than built — again.

items.title: DTCC and Euroclear become co-chairs of the Canton Foundation
items.entities: DTCC; Euroclear; Canton Foundation
items.summary: The incumbent depositories do not merely connect to the new network. They take the chair of the body that governs it.

items.title: Anchorage's USAT issuance policies take effect
items.entities: Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.; USAT
items.summary: The reserves sit in a segregated **South Dakota express trust** — legally separate from the OCC-chartered bank whose name is on the coin. Even inside one brand, the obligor is a different body from the bank.

items.title: The OCC conditionally approves five digital-asset trust banks in a single day
items.entities: OCC; Circle / First National Digital Currency Bank; Ripple National Trust Bank; BitGo; Fidelity Digital Assets; Paxos
items.summary: Five charters, one day, one agency — **the same agency that chartered the National Banks in 1863**. Conditional approval is not final approval, and final approval is not an open bank: each of the five must still satisfy pre-opening conditions, and each must separately apply for Federal Reserve Bank stock, which is a membership step and not an account.

items.title: Paxos Trust Company, N.A. — conversion effective at 5:00 p.m.
items.entities: OCC; Paxos Trust Company, N.A.
items.summary: The New York limited-purpose trust becomes a national trust bank at a stated hour — one of the very few births in this corpus that carries a clock. Not FDIC insured. No deposits. Expected to apply for Federal Reserve Bank stock. Marketed as "GENIUS-ready"; what is actually true is the conversion.

items.title: DTCC and Digital Asset announce a DTC Treasury-token path on Canton
items.entities: DTCC; DTC; Cede & Co.; Digital Asset; Canton Network
items.summary: The design, read carefully, is the opposite of the headline. The conventional position is **immobilised** in a Digital Omnibus Account; the securities stay registered to **Cede & Co.**; DTC mints token *representations* of participant entitlements and treats its LedgerScan record as **part of DTC's own official books**. Settlement is not digitised at launch. The chain is a transport surface. Title never leaves the building.

items.title: The Canton working group demonstrates a cross-border multi-asset repo
items.entities: Canton Network; LSEG Digital Settlement House; European government bonds; U.S. Treasuries
items.summary: European government bonds and U.S. Treasuries against euro and dollar cash, including **tokenized commercial-bank deposits** supplied through LSEG. Staged, real assets, working-group only — not an open market. Collateral is where the new stack becomes load-bearing, and this is what the frontier actually looks like.

items.title: BitGo Holdings lists on the NYSE
items.entities: BitGo Holdings, Inc. (BTGO); NYSE
items.summary: The custodian becomes a public company six weeks after its charter conversion is approved. Capital follows permission.

items.title: Ripple receives a full Electronic Money Institution licence in Luxembourg
items.entities: Ripple; Luxembourg (CSSF)
items.summary: The European door opens before the American one. Note what it is and is not: an EMI licence is not a bank charter, and Ripple's own aggregate count of "75+ licences globally" should never be read as 75 bank charters.

items.title: The OCC terminates Anchorage's 2021 operating agreement
items.entities: OCC; Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.
items.summary: The bank is found compliant with all ten actionable articles; the corrective actions are judged effective and sustainable. **The charter is not terminated — the leash is.** A supervisory release, and a real one. It changes nothing about the Federal Reserve request still sitting in the queue.

items.title: Bridge National Trust Bank receives preliminary conditional approval
items.entities: OCC; Bridge Ventures LLC; Stripe
items.summary: Stripe's stablecoin arm asks for a national trust charter and gets a conditional yes. The letter is explicit: pre-opening conditions must be met, the proposed bank **must apply for Federal Reserve Bank stock**, and none of this confirms a master account or authority to commence business.

items.title: The federal banking agencies clarify capital treatment for tokenized securities
items.entities: OCC; Federal Reserve; FDIC
items.summary: Tokenized securities generally take the **same capital treatment as the non-tokenized form**. A technical clarification, not a product approval — and precisely the kind of quiet ruling that lets an incumbent adopt the new wrapper without changing anything else.

items.title: Mastercard and SoFi announce they will explore SoFiUSD settlement
items.entities: Mastercard; SoFi Bank, N.A.; Galileo
items.summary: "Explore." Settlement, Multi-Token Network support and Galileo distribution are all described as *expected*, not completed. The verb is the whole story.

items.title: zerohash applies for a national trust bank charter
items.entities: OCC; zerohash
items.summary: An application, not an approval. As of the cutoff, no OCC decision has been located. zerohash already powers Morgan Stanley's E*Trade, Interactive Brokers Europe and a dozen other brands **without its name appearing anywhere the customer can see it** — which is exactly why its charter matters more than its profile.

items.title: Mastercard agrees to acquire BVNK for up to $1.8 billion
items.entities: Mastercard; BVNK
items.summary: The card network buys the adapter — enterprise fiat-to-stablecoin conversion and treasury orchestration — rather than building a coin. It integrates at the layer where the choosing happens: which issuers, which chains, which banks, which liquidity venues get distribution. Signed, not closed.

items.title: Coinbase National Trust Company receives preliminary conditional approval
items.entities: OCC; Coinbase Global; Coinbase National Trust Company
items.summary: Conditional only. The letter states in terms that the proposed trust has **no authority to commence business** until final approval. Coinbase did not open a national bank; Coinbase got in line.

items.title: Broadridge invests in HQLAx and announces a Canton migration path
items.entities: Broadridge; Digital Asset; HQLAx; Canton Network
items.summary: The production repo platform ties itself more tightly to the collateral registry and to Canton. Custody, settlement and migration milestones all remain future work — the investment is real, the plumbing is a plan.

items.title: J.P. Morgan's deposit token goes live on a public chain
items.entities: J.P. Morgan Chase Bank, N.A.; Kinexys; JPM Coin / JPMD; Base
items.summary: The bank exports a **commercial-bank deposit liability** onto a public network for eligible institutional clients — while keeping the deposit claim, the compliance perimeter, the client relationship and the ledger inside the bank. Native Canton issuance remains a planned 2026 path, not a verified production fact. This is the sharpest single answer to "who keeps the gate."

items.title: Visa reports a $7 billion annualized stablecoin settlement run rate
items.entities: Visa
items.summary: Nine chains, 130+ stablecoin-linked card programmes, 50+ countries, up 50% quarter on quarter. **Visa-defined programme metrics, not audited totals** — and not one gram of membership, netting, fraud or dispute authority has moved. The settlement asset became pluggable. The rulebook did not.

items.title: Paxos and BitGo appear on the OCC's active trust-bank list
items.entities: OCC; Paxos Trust Company, N.A. (charter 25379); BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. (charter 25366)
items.summary: Consummated. Two of the five December charters are now operating national trust banks with charter numbers. Neither has a confirmed Federal Reserve master account.

items.title: DTCC and Chainlink collaborate on 24/7 collateral management
items.entities: DTCC; Chainlink
items.summary: The Collateral AppChain is a *third* object — not DTC's entitlement-token service, not the Stellar connection. They may become interoperable. They do not share a ledger, a validator set, a legal operator, a cash asset or a rulebook merely because DTCC is in all three.

items.title: The SEC grants Paxos Securities Settlement Company temporary clearing-agency registration
items.entities: SEC; Paxos Securities Settlement Company, LLC (PSSC)

items.title: SoFiUSD launches — the first stablecoin issued by a U.S. national bank
items.entities: SoFi Bank, N.A.; Mastercard; Galileo
items.summary: The one clean vertical in the whole sweep: charter-holder, issuer and consumer brand are the same body. And the coin it issues **is not an insured deposit**. An FDIC-insured national bank can hand you two dollars with entirely different rights attached, and nothing at the counter tells you which one you are holding.

items.title: DTCC and the Stellar Development Foundation announce a planned connection
items.entities: DTCC; DTC; Stellar Development Foundation

items.title: The Federal Reserve access database: Anchorage still pending
items.entities: Federal Reserve; Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.
items.summary: The currency date of the public request database. Anchorage's request, filed nine months earlier, remains **pending**. No other member of the cohort has a publicly confirmed master account. The record shows a full waiting room and an unopened door.

items.title: FIUSD production target ("summer 2026")
items.entities: Fiserv; Paxos; Circle
items.summary: Slipped once already, from year-end 2025. The issuer, the redemption obligor, the reserve custodian and the first production users all remain unnamed in public documentation. Watch for a named debtor — until there is one, there is no coin.

items.title: MoneyGram launches MGUSD on Stellar
items.entities: MoneyGram; Bridge (issuer of record); M0; Fireblocks
items.summary: MoneyGram is the face. **Bridge** — which is Stripe — is the regulated issuer of record. M0 supplies the mint-and-burn logic. Three companies deep before you find out whose promise you are holding.

items.title: Mastercard expands settlement across multiple stablecoins and chains
items.entities: Mastercard; Circle (USDC); Paxos (PYUSD, USDG, USDP); Ripple (RLUSD); SoFi (SoFiUSD)
items.summary: Five issuers, eight chains — and Mastercard's fraud rules, dispute rules, participant structure and rulebook entirely intact. USDC carried early live flows; most of the rest was support and rollout, not proven volume. The network adopts tokenized cash **without yielding the customer or the constitution**.

items.title: Ripple reports RLUSD at $1.576 billion against $1.683 billion of reserves
items.entities: Ripple; Standard Custody & Trust Company; RLUSD
items.summary: Monthly CPA attestations, over-collateralised on the company's own numbers. A real regulated coin with a real reserve — issued by a **New York limited-purpose trust company**, not by the national bank Ripple has been conditionally approved to build.

items.title: DTC's preliminary tokenization service (stated window: second half of 2026)
items.entities: DTC; DTCC; Canton Network; Cede & Co.
items.summary: The December press release said the first half of 2026; DTC's own FAQ quietly moved it to the second half. **This lands in the same six months as the Treasury clearing mandate.** Watch the eligible CUSIPs, the first participant, the first transfer, the cash leg, and the correction path — the day a mistaken transfer must be undone is the day the new stack says out loud which ledger wins.

items.title: Swift says its blockchain ledger is ready for initial use
items.entities: Swift; ANZ; BNP Paribas; BNY; Citi; DBS; HSBC; Lloyds; MUFG; Standard Chartered; UBS; Wells Fargo (17 banks in total)
items.summary: Seventeen of the world's largest banks lined up to pilot — and what the ledger carries is **bank-issued tokenized deposits**, not public stablecoins. Final settlement still completes through the existing systems. The correspondent-banking guild did not surrender the rail. It built one, and kept the rulebook, the identity layer and the message standard it already owned.

items.title: Circle receives final OCC approval
items.entities: OCC; Circle Internet Group; First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A. (Circle National Trust)
items.summary: The first **final** — not conditional — approval in the cohort. And the gap that remains is the point: the opening date is unconfirmed, the transfer of reserve management is a planned future step, and **there is no confirmed Federal Reserve account**. Even the furthest-advanced charter in America has daylight between "final approval" and "open for business."

items.title: Custodia files its cert petition at the Supreme Court
items.entities: Custodia Bank; Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City; Supreme Court of the United States
items.summary: The Wyoming special-purpose depository institution takes the master-account question to the highest court. Fourteen chartered or approved bodies are standing in the same queue behind it. **This is no longer one bank's lawsuit — it is the load-bearing case of the entire private monetary stack.**

items.title: The wider OCC queue: a dozen more applicants nobody is naming
items.entities: OCC; World Liberty Trust Company; PAYO Digital Bank; zerohash national trust bank; Revolut Bank US; EDX Trust; Bastion Platforms; Lorum National Trust Bank; OpenReserve Bank; Agora National Trust Bank; Catena Trust Bank; Payward National Trust Company; CBW Bank
items.summary: The famous names are the visible part. The OCC's public digital-asset application list holds a far longer queue — a president's family venture, a British neobank, an exchange consortium, and a row of trust companies almost nobody has heard of. **A charter application is not an operating bank; a conditional approval is not a final one; and a trust charter is neither deposit insurance nor a Federal Reserve account.** The queue is the story.

items.title: Kraken's claimed Federal Reserve account is not in the public record
items.entities: Payward; Kraken Bank (Wyoming SPDI); Federal Reserve
items.summary: Kraken's group **states** that its Wyoming special-purpose depository holds a limited-purpose Federal Reserve account. The Fed's public access database does not corroborate it under any known Kraken or Payward name. Either Kraken is the first crypto-adjacent body through the door in American history, or the claim inflated in the telling. **Unconfirmed, and checkable** — which makes it a watch, not a finding.

items.title: The Ripple master-account claim is a conflation
items.entities: Ripple; Standard Custody & Trust Company; Federal Reserve; OCC
items.summary: The OCC's conditional-approval letter says the *proposed* Ripple National Trust Bank will apply for **Federal Reserve Bank stock** — a membership step. That is not a master-account request, and no Ripple or Standard Custody request was found in the Fed's public database. Membership, stock, a reserve account and a confirmed master account are four different things, and the retail story treats them as one.

items.title: Coinbase International Exchange consolidates into Deribit
items.entities: Coinbase; Deribit; Coinbase International Exchange
items.summary: Positions and balances migrate, subject to readiness and approvals. Global derivatives liquidity and risk concentrate into a single venue. Watch the legal novations, the risk-engine cutover and the insurance-fund treatment — concentration is only invisible until it isn't.

items.title: DTCC's Collateral AppChain (target: fourth quarter 2026)
items.entities: DTCC; Chainlink
items.summary: A separate object from the tokenization service. Watch asset eligibility, valuation, margin, the cash leg, and whether any of it carries production volume.

items.title: Mastercard's BVNK acquisition — outer bound of the stated closing window
items.entities: Mastercard; BVNK
items.summary: "Before year-end 2026." Until it closes, BVNK is a separate company. Watch the surviving legal entities, the licences, the safeguarding banks — and whether BVNK stays asset-neutral once a card network owns it.

items.title: DTC-tokenized assets on Stellar (target: first half of 2027)
items.entities: DTC; Stellar Development Foundation
items.summary: Watch the first eligible asset, the authoritative-record design, the cash leg, the corporate actions — and whether XLM has any role at all beyond paying for network function.

items.title: PSSC's temporary clearing registration reaches its outer limit
items.entities: SEC; Paxos Securities Settlement Company, LLC
items.summary: Eighteen months from the grant of 2026-05-27. Unless the Commission acts, the permission lapses. Watch permanent registration, scope changes, DTC membership — and the first default or recovery procedure, which is where a settlement system stops being a press release.
